Team — quick internal note and proposed legal framing before we send anything externally:

1) License scope: we can offer a limited-use license to ArcWell for artifacts produced via the private VPC deployment (snapshots, runbook excerpts, attestations) exclusively for business continuity and verification purposes. We should avoid granting a right to copy or distribute full model binaries. Redline will include a defined "Evidence Use" clause with a strict purpose and retention window.

2) Witness-lite escrow: Redwood is open to a custody-lite mechanism: staged sealed snapshots with an independent witness attestation (signed PDF) and an encrypted key escrow held by a third-party custodian. We will propose a narrow exhibit describing the trigger events for key release (e.g., prolonged vendor insolvency, failure to meet SLA for X days).

3) Evidence portal & runbook review: Ops to confirm what artifacts can be surfaced in a read-only staging area (we should limit to hash+metadata, curated runbook excerpts, and controlled log slices). David, please confirm the list of artifacts we can upload and the lifecycle (retention, access expiry) — I included a suggested minimal set in the attached redline doc.

4) Audit windows & witness statements: propose a single annual witness window by default, with a short, paid drill extension if the customer requests a live witness. Include sample witness statement language in the exhibit for quick acceptance.

David — see the attached Redwood_MSA_addendum_template_redline.docx. Jasmine — if Amanda agrees, we’ll produce an addendum that is (a) narrow in scope, (b) workable for procurement timelines, and (c) protects Redwood IP.
